subject: Re: Dedicated reserved pool — sizing, packaging and pricing clarification
body:
From: Ethan Moore <ethan.moore@skylineanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@skylineanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated reserved pool — sizing data and ask

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We’re close to an internal decision and need a concrete sizing and pricing proposal for a Dedicated (reserved) GPU pool we can present to our finance and procurement teams. Below is our expected workload profile; I attached a CSV with the per-endpoint breakdown. Please confirm whether the numbers below map to your recommended pool size and the preliminary committed pricing you showed.

Workload summary (current plan):
- Product: Conversational insights API (multi-turn chat + summarization)
- Peak concurrent users: 110 active sessions (peaks up to 160 for a few hours/day)
- Average concurrency to support: 120 sessions (planning safety buffer)
- Requests per second (steady): 60 QPS; peak burst: 180 QPS for 2–3 hours/day
- Average prompt context length: 1,200 tokens (including system+history)
- Average response tokens: 400 tokens
- Typical model: Llama-3-70B (quantized 4-bit), but we are open to alternatives.
- Latency SLO: 300ms 95th percentile for short replies (<=200 tokens); overall <500ms is desired.
- Monthly usage estimate: ~45M generated tokens (response tokens) + ~135M prompt tokens

We’d like:
- A recommended GPU pool (type + count) for steady throughput + burst plan.
- Expected steady throughput tokens/sec and how the pool handles KV cache for multi-turn sessions.
- Reserved commit pricing options (12 / 24 / 36 month) and any standard discounts or packaging (burst credits, overage rates).

Procurement would like an initial not-to-exceed monthly committed price and a best-effort discount if we commit to 24 months.

Thanks,
Ethan

---

On Wed, 25 Feb 2026 at 12:27 PM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:

Hi Ethan —

Thanks for the detailed profile and the CSV (received). I ran the numbers with Ben and attached a workbook that shows the assumptions and per-endpoint calculations. High-level thoughts up front:

1) Baseline recommendation (steady + headroom): 10x A100-80GB (or equivalent H100 pool) as a conservative starting point.
   - Rationale: with 1,600-token effective context (we simulate KV cache use) and 400 token average output, a single A100-80 can sustain roughly ~6–8 QPS for that model/precision when optimized and using continuous batching. That implies 10 GPUs -> ~70 QPS steady with caching benefits and batching; you’ll want additional headroom for your 180 QPS bursts.
2) Burst capacity: pair the reserved pool with a 4–6 GPU burst buffer (on-demand) to cover short peaks, or provision 2x the steady pool if you need hard guarantees for sustained peaks.
3) Concurrency handling: reward sessions that benefit from KV cache — we estimate a ~25–35% cost/latency improvement for hot conversations.

Pricing / commit structure (preliminary):
- 12-month commit: list price equivalent to $X per GPU/hour; typical discount 10% off hosted baseline pricing.
- 24-month commit: standard discount 18% (negotiable up to ~20% with an agreed rollout/milestone schedule).
- Overage & burst: overage billed at on-demand rate; a pool credit for monthly burst capacity can be included (we suggested 400 GPU-hours/month as a starting credit in the attachment).

Next steps: I’d like to confirm a few inputs (below) and then Ben will produce an updated price worksheet with concrete numbers.
- Can you confirm % of requests that are multi-turn (you noted conversational — is that 70%+?), and the expected average session length in turns?
- Do you expect model changes in the first 6 months (e.g., move to a smaller/faster model for embeds vs chat)?
- Any hard latency SLA requirements beyond what you wrote (for legal to evaluate)?

I’m looping in Ben (pricing) and Marissa (customer success) to align on rollout and SLA conversation.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx (workbook with assumptions and GPU-hour math)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved pool — sizing, packaging and pricing clarification

Ethan — quick note on the arithmetic and an alternative configuration.

We modeled two options in the attached sheet:
A) Performance-first (recommended for initial GA): 10x A100-80GB reserved + 6 GPU on-demand burst -> targets your 180 QPS peak with ~20% headroom. Expected steady throughput ~70 QPS given conservative batching.
B) Cost-first (trade latency): 7x H100-80GB (mixed precision) with more aggressive batching and quantization; this assumes you move to a slightly smaller custom quantized variant that reduces memory footprint. This lowers monthly committed spend ~18% vs A) but increases 95p latency by ~80ms in our sim.

Commit discounts we usually propose (baseline): 12-month = 12% off list for reserved pool; 24-month = 20% off; 36-month = 27% off (these are for pure reserved compute — additional discounts for longer deals or bundled telemetry/retention). Given you’re asking procurement for a 24-month sweet spot, I can draft a counter that holds 20% if we get an early payment milestone and a 12-month technical review.

I’ll attach a per-month invoice simulation and a short note on how overage is calculated (GPU-hours * on-demand $/hour).

-Ben

Attachment: skyline_workload_profile.csv, draft_terms_SKY-47.pdf

Thanks Ben — helpful. A couple of clarifications from procurement:
- They prefer a firm monthly committed price rather than GPU/hour line-items for comparison to other vendors. Can you provide an ARR or monthly committed cost (post-discount) for option A and B?
- They’re pushing for a 24-month commit. If Redwood can hold at 20% off list for 24 months, procurement will likely take it to execs — but they asked if we could see a more aggressive discount (22–25%) if Skyline agrees to a 36-month ramp with quarterly payments.
- SLA: They need a written latency objective (not strict SLA) in the quote: 95th < 350ms for the workloads described.

We’re less likely to change the model in the first 6 months — Llama-3-70B is the plan for initial GA. Multi-turns are ~72% of requests; typical session length 6–8 turns.

Ethan

On Fri, 27 Feb 2026 at 08:16 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:

Ethan / Procurement —

Appreciate the clarity. Ben and I discussed your ask for a single committed monthly price and a stronger term discount. See the attached revised quote table (sheet: "MonthlyCommitSummary"). Highlights:

- Option A (Performance-first): 10x A100-80GB reserved + 6 GPU on-demand buffer
  - Monthly committed price (24-month, 20% discount applied): $187,200/month (this normalizes to an hourly equivalent but gives procurement a single line item).
  - On-demand overage: $3.75/GPU-hour. We include 400 GPU-hours/month burst credit.
  - SLA objective: 95p latency <= 325ms for typical 400-token responses; we can include a 95p <=350ms contractual target in an appendix with agreed operational thresholds and penalty caps.

- Option B (Cost-first): 7x H100-ish equivalent (aggressive batching/quant)
  - Monthly committed price (24-month, 20% discount applied): $153,600/month.
  - Trade-offs: ~80–120ms added 95p latency in our sim and lower headroom for sustained peaks.

- 36-month acceleration discount: we can extend to 24% cumulative discount if Skyline commits to a 36-month contract with quarterly payments and a joint rollout plan (milestone at months 6 and 12 including traffic share and SLO review).

If procurement wants a 22–25% range immediately for 24 months, we’ll need to ask for a technical review clause and a modest annual commit ramp (first 6 months 70% of committed baseline). That would be our counter.

Marissa, from CS, will outline the onboarding timeline and an operational runbook for the rollout if Skyline lands on Option A.

Thanks,
Soojin

Hey Ethan — quick operational note from CS:

If you take Option A we can do a staged cutover over 8 weeks:
- Week 0–2: dedicated account setup, private VPC peering and IAM config
- Week 2–4: model onboarding and validation (we’ll run a full eval suite against your sample traffic)
- Week 4–6: canary traffic at 20–30% with auto-scaling thresholds monitored
- Week 6–8: full rollover and runbook handoff

We’ll provide: runbook, SRE contact list, observability dashboards (token-level cost, per-route latency), and a joint post-launch review at 30 days.

I’ll coordinate to capture the operational milestones in the contract appendix so procurement has measurable acceptance criteria.

Best,
Marissa
